(1) a blunt-needle injection is associated with lower rates of bruising than a sharp-needle injection; (2) a blunt-needled injection is associated with a lower risk of hematoma; (3) blunt-needled injections are associated with lower levels of pain; and (4) the use of a blunt-needling technique is associated with higher patient satisfaction.

(1) a 30-ga, 0.5-in needle is more effective than the control injection technique used by Yu in decreasing ecchymosis and (2) a 27-ga, 1.5-in blunt needle is not as effective as the control injection technique at reducing ecchymosis.

the use of a blunt-needle technique for anesthesia injection is more likely to result in bruising than the use of a sharp-needle technique, but it is less likely to result in hematoma formation and pain.

a 27-g needle cannula is superior to a 27-g sharp needle when used in the technique described by the authors.
the use of a blunt cannula for anesthetic injection is not superior to a 30-ga needle in reducing postoperative ecchrymotic complications.
a blunt-needle injection technique may decrease the risk of hematoma in the setting of upper eyelid blepharoplastics but does not decrease ecchymosis or postoperative pain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of hyaluronase, a topical anesthetic, and the use of a smaller, more controlled, needle injection technique can decrease postoperative ecchmyosis.

the use of hyaluronase and a single injection site, with anesthetic delivered slowly using a small-caliber (30-gauge), short (0.5 in) needle, is a more effective means of minimizing postoperative ecchrymosis than the use of a blunt cannula.
the use of a blunt cannula is associated with a higher rate of ecchmyosis than a 30-guage needle in upper blepharoplastics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the injection technique is a critical component of the procedure that can significantly impact the postoperative ecchmyosis and hematoma rates.
a 30-ga, 0.5-in needle with a 1:1 mixture of bupivacine and lidocaine supplemented with hyaluronadase is an effective means to decrease postoperative ecchmymosis.

a single entry site with the needle directed anteriorly, with the bevel up, in the subcutaneous plane just superficial to the orbicu-laris muscle is a safe, effective, and efficient means of delivering local anesthesia for the upper blepharoplastics.
